twins.concern: Feature instance text (<biological feature ID>@<record key>) and the CLI record key of a record input (record-<n>, record-<n>:<k> for an input that expands to several records)
twins.reason: A "This feature only" hash rule names one feature instance, which Python composes and matches whole. The Web reads the record key out of a rule at the separator and composes a rule naming another record key in the same function (namedFeatureInstance: Delete settings, Run Info, and a Generate that moves a record's rows to its new key), composes the CLI key record-<n> of the n-th record input in one function (cliRecordKey in services/record-draw-selection.js, which the Circular canvas key also uses), and composes the <key>:<k> record key of an expanding input in one function (expandedRecordKey: a Linear record identity, the request split of an ALL card, and the CLI record key that Run Info writes in the Source recipe -t table). The separator and the record key prefix and expansion separator are generated constants (tools/generate_web_contracts.py: FEATURE_INSTANCE_SEPARATOR, CLI_RECORD_KEY_PREFIX, EXPANDED_RECORD_KEY_SEPARATOR); the order of the parts is copied. tests/web/run-info.test.mjs runs the CLI on the rewritten table for a plain and an expanded record and checks that it colors one copy; no shared vector.
twins.retireWhen: Python writes the CLI form of the specific color table for the Source recipe and names the record of an instance row, so the Web neither parses nor composes an instance
twins.source: PR #1395 (feature-color-leak-20261026, REVIEW-2 item 1); the detector does not see it
